guide: Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: target litres per 100 km, the fleet figure for the fuel tax return, the card discount, the price alert limit and the plan for fuel cost per km.
Check Trucks, Drivers and Fuel Tax Regions. Put your own rated litres per 100 km and your own tax per litre in the yellow cells.
Enter every fill on Fuel Purchases. The amount, the net price, the km since the last fill, the litres per 100 km and the network check fill in by themselves.
Every week, enter the statement of the fuel card provider on Fuel Card Statements and read the check: a wrong price or a gap to your own fills shows in red.
Keep Fuel Price by Month and Station Price List current, and read Cheapest Stops by Lane before the dispatcher plans a load.
Enter the km and litres bought by region each quarter on Km and Litres by Region. Fuel Tax Return works out the net litres and the tax due or credit; Fuel Tax Filing Calendar tracks the due dates.
Log the bulk tank deliveries and issues on Bulk Tank Log, and the reefer unit hours on Reefer Fuel Use.
Follow the missing receipts on Missing Fuel Receipts and the card discount on Fuel Card Discounts until each one is closed.
Use Fuel Surcharge Recovered to compare the surcharge you billed with the extra fuel cost, and Fuel Budget to compare the plan with the real cost.
Take an odometer reading of every truck about once a month on Odometer Readings.

Use the 14 calculators: cost per km, litres per 100 km, net price, fuel tax, litres in a region, a cheaper stop, the surcharge needed, a bulk tank, reefer fuel, a trip budget, the card value, idling, a price swing and a what-if grid.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text already written (28 messages).
Read Fuel Dashboard and Charts every week: fuel cost, price, litres per 100 km, card discount, surcharge recovery and the fuel tax.

listing.headline: Know what every litre costs and what you owe in fuel tax
listing.description:
Run the fuel of a small carrier in one Excel workbook, from one owner-driver up to about eight trucks. Fuel Purchases holds every fill with its truck, driver, region, station, litres and price, and the amount, the net price after the card discount, the km since the last fill, the litres per 100 km and the fuel cost per km fill in by themselves.

Fuel Card Statements compares the weekly statement of your fuel card provider with the fills you entered, Fuel Card Discounts shows whether the discount was paid, and Missing Fuel Receipts follows every fill without a receipt until it is closed. Fuel Price by Month and Station Price List show the price swing by region and the stations that cost more than the average, and Cheapest Stops by Lane names the cheapest region on each lane with the saving per fill.

Km and Litres by Region feeds Fuel Tax Return, which works out the litres used, the net litres and the tax due or the credit for every region and quarter, and Fuel Tax Filing Calendar tracks the due dates and a return filed late. Fuel Use per Truck and Fuel Use per Driver rank litres per 100 km, Bulk Tank Log keeps the stock and its value, Reefer Fuel Use measures the refrigeration unit, Fuel Surcharge Recovered compares the surcharge you billed with the extra fuel cost, and Fuel Budget and Odometer Readings finish the picture.

14 calculators cover cost per km, litres per 100 km, net price, fuel tax by region, litres in a region, a cheaper stop, the surcharge needed, a bulk tank, reefer fuel, a trip budget, the card value, idling, a price swing and a what-if grid. Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and send 28 ready messages with the details already written in.

This is part three of the Trucking suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, 15 languages in one purchase, with a demo copy full of sample data for a small fleet to explore first. Fuel tax rates are demo inputs: check your own rates. Money is shown in one plain currency and distances in km or miles. It helps you plan and does not promise results.
